title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is page 1 of 33 and sets up the arithmetic framework for the 'paradigmes des courbes algébriques'.

§1. Let X̄ be a scheme over Q̄ ⊂ C, and let 𝒢_X̄ = Aut(X̄) be its automorphisms as an absolute scheme, i.e. Q̄-semilinear automorphisms. An absolute automorphism induces an automorphism of the base Q̄, provided Q̄ is intrinsically recognisable in Γ(X̄,O). This holds, for example, when X̄ is connected and non-empty, which is presumably what the margin note says. One then gets an exact sequence
 1 → G_X̄ = Aut(X̄/Q̄) → 𝒢_X̄ → Γ = Gal(Q̄/Q).
Grothendieck asks in the margin: is the last map surjective? Is there an example where it is not?

In modern terms, the image of 𝒢_X̄ → Γ is the group of σ with X̄^σ ≅ X̄. Its fixed field is the field of moduli M of X̄, so the sequence is
 1 → Aut(X̄) → 𝒢_X̄ → Gal(Q̄/M) → 1.

By infinite Galois theory, subfields K ↔ closed subgroups Γ_K, with K finite over Q iff Γ_K has finite index. A K-model of X̄ ('restriction du corps de base') gives a continuous lift Γ_K → 𝒢_X̄ of the inclusion Γ_K ⊂ Γ. That is a section over Γ_K, i.e. a Weil/Galois descent datum.

Conversely, the lift should determine the model. The text says 'if X̄ is reduced (?) and locally of finite type'. Grothendieck circles the '?' and writes 'effectivité de l'hypothèse' in the margin, showing awareness that descent effectivity is at issue.

Corollary: if X̄ is of finite type, it is defined over a number field K. Hence the image of 𝒢_X̄ → Γ contains Γ_K and has finite index, i.e. the field of moduli is a number field.

§2 (continued on the next page). Assume X connected and non-empty. Take a universal cover X̃ → X and let ℰ_X be the group of absolute automorphisms of X̃ lifting automorphisms of X. This gives an extension
 1 → π_1(X̄) → ℰ_X → 𝒢_X → 1.
Over the stabiliser 𝒢_X(ξ) of a Q̄-point ξ, it splits once X̃ is pointed over ξ; otherwise the splitting is defined only up to inner automorphisms from π_1.

This generalises the familiar picture 1 → π_1(X̄) → π_1(X_K) → Γ_K → 1 with its outer Galois action. Here the arithmetic Galois group is replaced by the bigger 'absolute symmetry group' 𝒢_X̄, which mixes geometric automorphisms and Galois. This is the setting needed for curves that are not defined over their field of moduli and for the Galois action on Teichmüller-type towers.
errors: The map 𝒢_X̄ → Γ is not defined for arbitrary X̄. It needs Q̄ to be canonically determined in Γ(X̄,O), e.g. X̄ connected and non-empty. For X̄ = Spec Q̄ ⊔ Spec Q̄, the swap composed with (σ,τ), σ≠τ, induces no element of Γ. Grothendieck only adds 'connexe ≠ ∅' in §2; the margin note may be addressing exactly this.

The claim that the lift Γ_K → 𝒢_X̄ 'defines' the K-structure needs effectivity of Galois descent. That is guaranteed for quasi-projective (or affine) X̄, not for an arbitrary scheme locally of finite type. Grothendieck crossed out 'quasi-proj' and marks the issue with '?' and 'effectivité'.
Reducedness is not the relevant hypothesis (the circled '?' suggests he doubted it). Continuity of the action plus quasi-projectivity is what matters.
The marginal question 'surjectif ? exemple où non surj. ?' has an immediate answer: any variety whose field of moduli is not Q, e.g. an elliptic curve with j ∉ Q.

ideas.what: Group of absolute (semilinear) automorphisms of a Q̄-scheme and the exact sequence 1 → Aut(X̄/Q̄) → Aut_abs(X̄) → Gal(Q̄/Q)
ideas.modern_name: Group of semilinear automorphisms; its image defines the field of moduli
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil (descent, 1956); Matsusaka, Shimura (field of moduli); later Coombes–Harbater 1985, Dèbes–Douai 1997
ideas.where_published: Implicit in SGA1 descent formalism; Esquisse d'un programme discusses Galois actions on moduli/dessins

ideas.what: K-forms ↔ continuous sections Γ_K → 𝒢_X̄ (effective for quasi-projective X̄)
ideas.modern_name: Weil/Galois descent; field of definition vs field of moduli obstruction
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. VIII; FGA (Technique de descente)

ideas.what: The image of 𝒢_X̄ → Γ has finite index for X̄ of finite type
ideas.modern_name: Field of moduli is a number field

ideas.what: Extension 1 → π_1(X̄) → ℰ_X → 𝒢_X → 1 of the absolute automorphism group by the geometric π_1, split over point stabilisers (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Arithmetic fundamental group of the 'field-of-moduli' quotient; enlarged fundamental exact sequence incorporating Aut(X̄)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1 fundamental exact sequence) in the Galois case; enlarged versions in Dèbes–Douai, Dèbes–Emsalem, and anabelian literature
ideas.where_published: SGA1 IX (Galois-only version); Esquisse/letter to Faltings use outer actions

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly frames anabelian/'paradigm' questions around the full absolute automorphism group 𝒢_X̄ ⊃ Aut(X̄/Q̄), not just Γ_K. He also treats the extension by π_1 split only over point stabilisers. This anticipates the field-of-moduli formalism of Dèbes–Douai, but it is a natural setup rather than a new result.
missed.quote: on considère le groupe 𝒢_X̄ des automorphismes de X̄ en tant que schéma absolu
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mildly relevant: a historical precursor to the treatment of field of moduli vs field of definition inside anabelian geometry. No new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an opening set-up page: semilinear automorphism groups, Galois descent, and finiteness of the field of moduli are all standard. Only the framing (the absolute automorphism group extended by π_1 as the basic object for 'paradigmes des courbes') is of historical interest.
transcription_corrections: 'À une restriction des groupes de base' should read 'À une restriction du corps de base Q̄ de X̄ à K'. The image reads 'des gorps de base', i.e. corps.

The margin note near (2)/(3) likely reads roughly: 'Q̄ ↪ Γ(X, O_X), il faut [que Q̄ soit la clôture alg.] de Q [dans Γ(X,O_X)], p.ex. ...'. In other words, it is a condition ensuring 𝒢 → Γ is well defined. The machine transcription's fragmentary reading is uncertain.
Diagram (4) is a lift Γ_K → 𝒢_X̄ over the inclusion Γ_K ⊂ Γ (the arrow goes from Γ_K up to 𝒢_X̄), not a statement '𝒢 → Γ, Γ ⊃ Γ_K'.

The left margin note near (4) reads approximately 'grandes classes d'effectivité de qq. propriétés des groupes de déf.' and the one above (4) reads 'effectivité de l'hypothèse'. Both concern effectivity of descent.
In §2 the struck phrase is 'Considérons un revêtement universel X̃ →p X' and 'et' is replaced by '≠ ∅' (i.e. 'X connexe ≠ ∅').
